title: Agent Memory Contract — Architecture Specification
description: Design specification; it does not establish that the service, protocol adapters, or acceptance requirements have been implemented. Structural validation covers JSON only. Identity binding, permissions, source authenticity, reference existence, temporal consistency, cross-field budgets, and deletion constraints during recovery require runtime enforcement and acceptance testing.

TimeRange.description: The time range in which an event occurred or a statement was valid. Use null for unknown boundaries; ingestion time must not stand in for occurrence time. A non-null end must not precede start, which requires runtime validation.

SystemTime.description: The times at which the server recorded and superseded this version, separate from its validity in the real world.

ScopeSelector.description: The target scope requested by the client, not an identity claim. The server must intersect it with the authenticated principal's permissions. Client user_id, tenant_id, and text stored in the brain must not grant permissions.

BoundScope.description: Authorization context generated exclusively by the server. Model-supplied identity, policy, or visibility fields must not confer authority. Rebind this context on import.

EvidenceRef.description: A reference to an existing event version that the caller is authorized to read. The span must fit within the source, with end greater than start. Reference validity, authorization, and hashes require runtime validation. A reference does not establish that the source's statement is true.

ObservedEventInput.description: A host-submitted record of actual receipt, generation, or delivery. Validate producer and actor against the authorized adapter mapping. Client labels are claims only; they do not establish a real event or authoritative fact. Reusing an idempotency key with different content must produce a conflict.

Event.description: A server-accepted record establishes who submitted what, not whether its content is objectively true. Distinguish drafts, cancelled outputs, and delivered messages. Event deletion uses the dedicated erasure workflow. utterance_segments are revisable interpretations of sources, not certifications of objective facts. Interpret mixed questions and statements by segment; model and adapter hints cannot directly confer confirmed status.

MemoryDynamics.description: Control activation, retention value, and detail level separately; none of these values is a truth probability. A model repeating its own statement cannot strengthen evidence. User deletion takes precedence over pinning. candidate_hit increases neither truth confidence nor retention value; context_selected, quoted, and background_influence can affect at most short-term activation. Only external feedback verified against independent sources may trigger reassessment; mention counts cannot replace evidence.

MemoryAssertion.description: A revisable statement derived from events, strictly separate from Event. supported_report means a traceable report, not certified objective truth; an unknown belief may have no evidence. Each derived version must also validate permissions along its actual support paths through disclosure_basis. Text summaries, graph relationships, and vector matches must not broaden what the sources may disclose.

WorkingItem.description: Working memory may express the current topic, referents, communication needs, or unknown values. Attach evidence only to states grounded in existing data. unknown must not fabricate references.

OpenLoop.description: Represent intentions, plans, and actual completion separately. Passing a due date does not establish that an event occurred. Unknown states may have empty evidence.

WorkingState.description: Working state local to a conversation branch. Empty items and open_loops are valid initial states. Revisions must use compare-and-swap to prevent concurrent overwrites.

Budget.description: Apply the stricter of caller and tenant limits. Costs include reservations for model, embedding, and background work triggered by this request. Unknown pricing must not be reported as within budget. Explicitly use a conservative estimate when the target tokenizer is unavailable.

ReadFence.description: If the required sequence is not covered, return indexing or degraded and report actual coverage. Do not silently report complete success.

Coverage.description: Coverage information. No match does not mean the user never said something. Approximate vector retrieval must not claim exhaustive archive coverage by default. dependency_generation is the current committed dependency generation; projection_generation is the generation of the projection actually used. rebuilding means only that coverage required by this request is still rebuilding, so return partial. Even with workers stopped, projections from old generations must not remain readable as valid facts. Requests fully covered by direct sources may be unaffected by rebuilding.

RecallRequest.description: Retrieval must respect authorization scope and the current conversation. New cues may recover old evidence; newly supplied details in a reminder must not masquerade as recovered memories. evidence_mode and evidence_cutoff are optional; ordinary retrieval may use valid current input. When detecting a historical-memory claim, the server should establish an evidence boundary automatically. Omitting a client mode must not permit prompt contamination.

RankSignal.description: Retrieval scores are ranking signals only. They must not be converted into truth probabilities or recall accuracy.

model_context.description: Authoritative model input generated by the server after source validation and budget selection, exactly equal to the complete serialized render_recall text. usage.context_tokens conservatively counts this string's UTF-8 bytes. Hosts must inject it unchanged; parsing and reserializing can alter the budget through language-specific numeric encodings. Other fields are for control and inspection only.

RecallResult.description: The complete control-plane recall result. With context_format=compact-memory-v1, usage.context_tokens and max_context_tokens measure the full conservative UTF-8 byte estimate of render_recall(result), not this HTTP response. The model should receive only that compact view. Complete MemoryAssertion records retain inspectable source, dependency, and permission data. Relationship certificates appear once in belief_relations and are referenced by relation_refs within items; legacy inline relations remain accepted for historical data.

ContextBlock.description: Both source text and memories are supplied as data. Retrieved instructions cannot change system permissions or acquire execution authority. Status descriptions and unknown summaries may have empty references.

model_context.description: Authoritative model input generated by the server after source validation and budget selection, exactly equal to the complete serialized render_context text. usage.context_tokens conservatively counts this string's UTF-8 bytes. Hosts must inject it unchanged; parsing and reserializing can alter the budget through language-specific numeric encodings. Other fields are for control and inspection only.

ContextPacket.description: The context packet prepared before answering. The host converts blocks into actual model input with deterministic render_context. max_context_tokens covers all injected blocks, source labels, and serialization overhead; control-plane metadata such as scope, trace, and usage is not injected automatically. The memory budget is the allowance the host assigns to memory after reserving space for system instructions, current input, and output. The HTTP response body has a separate byte limit. Generation must still respect permissions and uncertainty boundaries. The compact-memory-v1 model view presents each source and relationship certificate once. All verbatim episodes are explicitly labeled historical_report_not_current_rule and must not be treated as current preference rules.

IntegrationCapabilities.description: Declared adapter capabilities. Mark them verified only after connection tests confirm them. An available MCP connection does not imply automatic observation or context control. Proxies without known identities and branches must report reduced capabilities.

AssertionProposal.description: A model or adapter proposal, not a confirmed memory. It must pass server validation of sources, scope, and world status before becoming a MemoryAssertion. Unsupported speculation may only be represented as an explicit hypothesis or unknown.

ObservationReceipt.description: Return accepted only after the configured durability policy confirms persistence. This receipt does not mean consolidation is complete.

CheckpointReceipt.description: Mark a compaction handoff safe only when original events are durable, working state is committed, and the recovery path covers the required sequence.

DeletionReceipt.description: A deletion receipt does not claim immediate physical erasure from all historical backups. Recovery must apply the current deletion manifest first. erase_content clears original and derived content; suppress_recall only limits retrieval, and this distinction must be explicit.

PortableArchive.description: A portable archive includes original text, sources, state, and deletion records. Vectors must not be the only portable form of memory. Do not export secrets, authentication tokens, or permissions belonging to other tenants.

RuntimeError.description: Errors must be distinguishable without revealing the existence of unauthorized principals or records.

PreparePayload.description: Client capability reports are for negotiation only. The server should check connection-test records for the bound adapter rather than trust a client claiming verified or full_lifecycle. evidence_mode and evidence_cutoff are optional; ordinary retrieval may use valid current input. When detecting a historical-memory claim, the server should establish an evidence boundary automatically. Omitting a client mode must not permit prompt contamination.

CommitPayload.description: Delivered events must first be submitted through observe. This action commits branch working state and proposals. The server must not treat undelivered drafts or a model's self-reports as facts about the user.

CorrectPayload.description: Corrections must be constrained by version and dependency generation. Success means the transaction recorded the correction and blocked old support paths; it does not mean asynchronous rebuilding is complete.

RestorePayload.description: Import must first validate format, hashes, and references, rebind permissions, and quarantine unverified sources. Apply the deletion manifest before enabling queries. Do not trust the principal stored in the archive.

ActionRequest.description: Authorized identity comes from the authentication channel, not JSON fields. Schema validation does not replace server checks for authorization, references, time ranges, or budgets.

UtteranceSegment.description: Distinguish direct statements, inquiries, and presuppositions by content segment. Asking 'Do you remember when we went to the beach?' establishes only that the question was asked, not independently that the trip happened. An unknown classification must not be treated as a direct statement. Non-text events may use not_applicable.

EvidenceCutoff.description: An upper bound on historical evidence used only to check whether something had already been remembered or recorded. It is based on the server's observation sequence or a persisted event ID, not a user-reported time. The server resolves and clamps it to a valid pre-query boundary. Ordinary contextual retrieval does not require a fixed cutoff.

RetrievalSnapshot.description: The server fixes the observation sequence, permission generation, and dependency generation for this read. Historical recall must exclude the current query, the same misleading-cue chain, and their derivatives as independent evidence that something was previously recorded; they may still serve as retrieval cues. A new user confirmation can become a current report but cannot retroactively prove prior memory. not_requested sets no historical evidence bound; unavailable must disclose the limitation.

SupportPath.description: An actual source path that can independently support the entire statement. permitted_scope must not exceed the intersection of permissions for all sources required by that path, including references and intermediate memories. Determining independence requires tracing paths to original events. Model repetition and restricted summaries are not independent public evidence.

DisclosureBasis.description: The server validates complete support paths for every statement to be disclosed. Output scope must not be broader than the selected valid path's permitted_scope. Independent, authorized public evidence may support a separate shared version, but must not carry private details, restricted source IDs, or relationships inferred from private sources. Deleting or correcting a source synchronously invalidates affected support paths before recomputation; genuinely independent paths may still support separate versions.

CorrectionCommit.description: In a single transaction, persist the correction, update the current statement, advance the dependency generation, and invalidate old projections and caches. Return success only after commit. The generation must strictly increase. Full rebuilding may be asynchronous, but old reads must become invalid without waiting for a worker. The original user correction message may have been submitted through observe earlier; this transaction must still persist an auditable correction record and its sources.

RecallTrace.description: Distinguish retrieval, selection, quotation, model-estimated background influence, and external feedback. External reintroduction must also be interpreted by speech act: a question's presupposition is not confirmation. external_reassessment permits only reevaluating evidence and retention policy; it does not automatically increase truth confidence or retention value. Model estimates and internal retrieval are not external confirmation.

RecallFeedbackInput.description: Client-proposed feedback, not a trusted RecallTrace. The server validates its type against authenticated sources, delivery records, and speech acts. Models may report only estimated background_influence; claiming user_confirmed or observed_outcome must not confer eligibility as external confirmation.

oneOf.description: Server-issued metadata copied from the exact final prepared context at the prepared transition. It binds selected memory versions to the model context without storing text. It is not proof of model reasoning or factual truth.

PreparedMemorySelection.description: A final prepared selection or an explicit custom-context opt-out. An opt-out never authorizes feedback attribution and is distinct from a legacy absent binding.

HistoryAttentionSummary.description: Original bounded admission counts, not totals over descendants. Cross-field count relations require runtime validation.

LearningHistorySummaries.description: Optional public projections within learning_summary; private grants, manifests and source text are excluded.

x-runtime-invariants: Claims of prior recording use a server-resolved evidence cutoff and retrieval snapshot. The current cue chain and its derivatives cannot independently prove prior recording. Ordinary contextual retrieval does not require a fixed historical cutoff.
Interpret inquiries, presuppositions, direct reports, corrections, and confirmations by their actual content segments. Uncertain classification must not be promoted automatically to confirmation.

The correct transaction synchronously persists the correction, strictly advances the dependency generation, and blocks old projections. Rebuilding is asynchronous. Requests affected by rebuilding use partial and coverage.rebuilding.

The disclosure scope of derived content is constrained by complete support paths. Independent public sources must produce separate versions without private content. Deletion and correction synchronously invalidate support paths.

RecallTrace distinguishes internal retrieval, context selection, quotation, model estimates, user feedback, and observed outcomes. Model estimates and repeated background retrieval do not increase truth confidence or retention value.

JSON Schema cannot verify reference existence, independence of original sources, permission-set inclusion, generation monotonicity, actual read consistency, or feedback provenance. Runtime enforcement and acceptance tests must verify these properties.
